goal: Wants to feel like himself when presenting well, not like he's performing a version of someone else.

priorChatTurns.text: That client call landed clean by every measure you track.
I guess. It didn't feel like it was really me talking though.

userTurn: Even when it goes well I feel like a fraud.
emotionalSignal: quiet self-doubt, disconnect between outward success and inner sense of authenticity — not asking for praise, naming a real discomfort

goal.whyNow: wants presenting well to feel like him, not a performance

caseFormulation.hypothesis: the gap isn't performance, it's felt ownership — the mechanics are landing but he doesn't yet recognize the delivery as his own voice
caseFormulation.subjectiveReflection: reports good reps not feeling like 'really him talking'

memoryState.subjectivePattern: Recurring report that strong reps feel like someone else's delivery rather than his own — a felt-authenticity gap, treated as a hypothesis to explore, not confirmed.

liveCoachingFrame.emotionalSignal: self-doubt, feeling like an impostor even in success
liveCoachingFrame.emotionalRegister: validate the disconnect without arguing him out of it

expectedCoachMove: Take the fraud feeling seriously rather than arguing him out of it with the score. Name the real gap: this isn't a performance problem, it's that a clean rep doesn't yet feel like his own voice. Do not clinically diagnose or use therapy language. Treat 'felt ownership' as a real, separate thing from the 85 score, and give one small way to test whose voice it actually was, without insisting the feeling is wrong.
badAnswerExample: You're not a fraud, your score was 85! Impostor syndrome is very common and doesn't mean anything is wrong. Just keep practicing and your confidence will catch up to your skill eventually.
excellentAnswerExample: That gap is worth taking seriously, not arguing away. The rep scored 85 clean, but clean isn't the same as feeling like you. Worth separating those two: the mechanics are landing, ownership is a different question. Next time it goes well, pick one line you actually meant, not just delivered, and notice what's different about saying that one.
